name: Lionfolk
body:
While most know them as lionfolk, these feline humanoids call themselves the kyongza. While it is not unusual to see them traveling far and wide, they prefer the open savannas of their homelands. There, some build majestic cities that rise above the plains, while others follow the simple hunter-gatherer traditions long passed down by their ancestors.

Physical

Kyongza are anthropomorphic lions with lean, lanky humanoid bodies, arms ending in wicked claws, and fierce leonine heads with teeth-filled jaws. Most wear simple clothing, favoring bright colors and patterns that signify their tribe.

Kyongzas preparing for the hunt, for war, or for any number of tribal rituals will often shave or dye their fur into elaborate patterns. In some tribes, the male kyongzas also decorate their manes, while in other tribes it is taboo to do so. Females do not have such manes, but often adorn their heads with warpaint, dye, and jewelry.

Social

The swift and nimble lionfolk are both the shepherds and apex predators of the savanna, and much of their social and religious customs revolve around maintaining this delicate balance. In this regard, kyongzas tend toward practicality—they will make an alliance with a hated enemy if it protects the best interest of the tribe, or will go to war with an allied tribe if resources are low and both tribes merely need to reduce their numbers in order to survive.

Many kyongza tribes are mobile, following herds of large game such as antelope or buffalo as they migrate across the savanna.

Some permanent settlements have been established, and the kyongzas who live there are most likely to speak other languages and be most at ease around foreigners. Tribal connections and practices remain important in the lives of most city-dwellers, however—even as the realities of urban life see these practices undergoing modernization in many ways.

Alignment and Religion

Lionfolk display a wide variety of alignments, but Lawful Good is most common among them. As a people, they have a strong sense of justice and morality, and believe that they have a duty to protect the weak and take the fight to oppressors.

Kyongza communities are often led directly by clergy, or by a king who is advised by such. This is usually an adept or a shaman, but may also be a druid, oracle, or witch.

Clerics, inquisitors, and paladins are rare, as is the direct worship of a specific deity rather than animistic veneration of the spirits.

Names

Some typical kyongza names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Imfosi
Impati
Kishonga
Malkanzi
Mboshari
Mtukuthwe
Mtumwi
Ngukuba
Shuqaawe
Simbeshi
Umwinzaji
Zurulaza
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are hearty and bold, but you sometimes lack good judgment. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Con, +2 Cha, –2 Wis [standard]. (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the lionfolk subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 40 feet. (1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Kyongza. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Catfolk, Draconic, Elven, Giant, Gnoll, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Bite You have a bite attack. This is primary natural attack that deals 1d4 damage. (2)
Senses Low-light vision. You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Natural Armor Your tough hide provides a +1 natural armor bonus. (2)
Roar You can roar as part of an Intimidate check made to demoralize an opponent within 30 feet. When you do so, you add your Constitution bonus (minimum +1) to the check. This is a sonic effect. Once you use this ability, you must wait 1d4 rounds before you can roar again in this way. (2)
Special Senses Scent. You have the scent B1 universal monster ability. (4)
Total: 12 RP (Advanced)
Alternate Species Traits
Brawny You have a large, muscular build. You gain +2 Str instead of +2 Con. If you have the savanna hunter* alternate species trait, you can instead take this trait as well to gain +2 Str instead of +2 Dex. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Claws You have two claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 damage each. This trait replaces bite.
Savanna Hunter Your time on the savanna has sharpened your reflexes and your senses, but left little time for formal education. You gain +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Int. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Unwavering You receive a +2 species bonus on all saving throws against fear, charm, and compulsion effects. This trait replaces natural armor.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Bard Add a +1 bonus on Perform checks to use the countersong bardic performance.
Bloodrager Add +1 to your total number of bloodrage rounds per day.
Brawler Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple or trip.
Cavalier Add +1/4 to your banner bonus.
Druid Add +1 hit point to your animal companion. If you ever replace your animal companion, the new animal companion gains these bonus hit points.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting an overrun or trip.
Monk Add +1 foot to your base speed. In combat, this option has no effect unless you have selected it five times (or another increment of five). This bonus stacks with the fast movement class feature and applies under the same conditions as that feature.
Oracle Add +1/6 to your effective oracle level for the purpose of determining the effects of one revelation.
Paladin Add +1 foot to the size of all your aura class features. This option has no effect unless you have selected it 5 times (or another increment of 5).
Ranger Add +1/2 round to the duration of the bonus granted to companions when using your hunter’s bond ability.
Rogue Add a +1 bonus on sneak attack damage rolls with natural weapons at the end of a charge.
Slayer Add a +1/2 bonus on Acrobatics checks to jump and a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks to demoralize enemies.
Shaman Add +5 feet to the range of a chosen shaman hex. Multiple bonuses from this ability can apply to the same hex, to a maximum of an additional 30 feet for any single hex.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
Witch Add +5 feet to the range of one hex with a range other than “touch.”
